overview: A dark, highly theatrical home-video anthology by the Italian shock-rock pioneers Death SS. Directed by acclaimed multimedia artist Alessandro Amaducci, this release captures the conceptual heights of the band's legendary "Panic" album era.  Far from a standard, straightforward concert film, the feature seamlessly blends cinematic promotional music videos with heavily choreographed live studio performances recorded at the CTM Theatre in Rezzato, Italy. Featuring the band's polished studio recordings overlaid onto raw, occult stage visuals, the songs are stitched together with backstage tour diaries, fan interactions, and macabre interludes. It serves as the ultimate visual tribute to frontman Steve Sylvester's "Panic Theater"—a wild mix of classic heavy metal, gothic horror aesthetics, and provocative stage performance that perfectly defines the band's cult legacy.

title: Aftermass: Bicycling in a Post-Critical Mass Portland
original_title: Aftermass: Bicycling in a Post-Critical Mass Portland
overview: The world looks to Portland, Oregon as an example of how bicycle culture can blossom out of the ruinous freeways of car-oriented civilization. Aftermass is the first feature documentary to explore the events, people, politics, and social changes that led to Portland becoming the first major bicycle city in the United States. Aftermass features many of the leaders and major participants behind the growth of bicycling ridership since 1971. The narrative demonstrates the complex dynamic throughout the 1990s between advocacy organizations, politicians, city planners, and the then new, grassroots Critical Mass ride. The film is full of smiling faces on two wheels, but also explores the controversies, setbacks, and bumps along the way, including riots, political roadblocks, and an illegal police spy.

title: INTERSTICE
overview: INTERSTICE explores time as a layered and nonlinear element. A found film test—a seemingly fixed moment—is manipulated through scratching, re-photographing, looping, and additional animation to disrupt and reshape its temporal continuity. The direct animation, if projected traditionally, would transpire subliminally. But by creating loops within loops, new interactions between frames are revealed. The figure becomes a spectral presence, caught between motion and stillness—like a fleeting thought or memory folding back on itself. Time becomes elastic, with moments repeating, shifting, and evolving rather than progressing forward. The result is a meditation on motion, memory, and the fluidity of perception.

title: SCAPES

Each scene invites viewers to journey through layers of color and motion, where isolated elements feel intricately connected.  Through a combination of dynamic animation and tactile stop-motion, “Scapes” blurs the boundaries between organic and constructed, evoking a sense of wonder, discovery, and timelessness within its richly layered realities.

title: silver like dust
overview: A 16mm exploration of religion, trauma, and material filmmaking. Hand developed in home-made caffenol solutions, hand animated frame by frame.  a shout into the thunderous silence, a need for answers  An environmentally conscious choice to develop in as non-toxic a solution as possible left indelible marks and layers on the film. The film was discovered in Gosfilmofond of Russia during an examination of the uncatalogued portion of the foreign film collection. It had been listed under its German release title, Ein zerstörtes Leben (A Shattered Life), which had led to its initial classification as a German production. Subsequent identification established that it was in fact the American film Entangled Lives, produced by Edwin Thanhouser’s (1865–1956) film company and previously believed to be lost. People in the small border town once grew up together, and the relationship between Hou Xiaochuan and the young gangsters today is just like the situation of the young Hou Yu 30 years ago. But his father used to bear it all the time, fearing the consequences of rebellion, and was still treated like an ant in the drinking game as an adult. Now Hou Xiaochuan does not want to repeat his father's mistakes. He wants to let those domineering people know that the so-called consequences should be borne by them.

overview: The Watergate Caper is an archival documentary, narrated by Harry Shearer (This is Spinal Tap), tracing the rise and fall of Nixon from the presidential primaries of 1968 through the Watergate break-in of June 1972 to his resignation two years later, killing trust in the political process and the American presidency in the wake of the Vietnam War.  The film draws on hundreds of hours of TV news taped off-air by the Nixon White House to tell the untold story of the Watergate burglars. How did tapping the wrong phone with a bug that didn't work lead to their arrests and Nixon's resignation? overview: What is a quilt? This episode introduces the audience to the brave new world of the American quilt, where that question has many different answers. If a ‘real’ quilt is a three-layer fabric sandwich sewn together and folded over a bed, how do we define the quilt that is an amalgamation of fabric, photography, print making and other media, and hangs on a gallery wall? Our experts contribute varying perspectives, setting the stage for the complexity of the series’ larger topic: Why quilts matter and how they relate to history, art and politics. This episode also takes a look at judgments of quality in the quilt world. Learn what makes one antique quilt more valuable and important than another, and why contemporary quilts are judged by a very different set of standards. To close the episode, experts provide practical suggestions for quilt fans who want to develop their ‘eye’ for a great quilt. In short, it’s Quilts 101, and the perfect introduction to a surprisingly complex subject.

These images or scenes are unsettling not only because they break the ‘sacred’ fourth wall, but above all because Seidl makes the viewer complicit. The protagonists look directly into your eyes. title: The History of Toys and Games
original_title: The History of Toys and Games
overview: Actor John Ritter ("Three's Company") hosts this fun look at America's favorite playthings. From the humble, hand-crafted objects that occupied Colonial children to the complex video games of the '90s, toys and games hold a special place in the nation's collective heart. Archaeological digs have turned up little wooden tops, whistles and corn-husk dolls that once gave children a way to cope with harsh everyday realities. Today children still love their now mass-produced delights. The History of Toys and Games follows the progress of fun pastimes and introduces the fascinating inventors who've created and marketed this century's most popular toys - including Barbie, Lionel Trains, Crayola Crayons, Erector Sets, Hot Wheels, Play Doh, PEZ and Mr. Potato Head.

title: NEVER GIVE UP: The Adam Wardzinski Story
original_title: NEVER GIVE UP: The Adam Wardzinski Story
overview: For years, Adam stood outside the traditional power centers of jiu-jitsu, carving his own path from Poland to the world's biggest stages. While others followed established systems, Adam developed a style uniquely his own, an unpredictable, pressure-filled game built around creativity, intelligence, and an almost obsessive understanding of the art.  Behind the medals, the victories, and the countless hours spent on the mats is a husband, a father, a teacher, and a man deeply connected to the people and places that shaped him. His pursuit of greatness exists alongside the responsibilities of family, the weight of representing his country, and the question of what it truly means to dedicate a life to a craft.  This is not simply the story of how Adam Wardziński became a champion.  It is the story of how one man forged his own path and, in doing so, helped put Polish jiu-jitsu on the world stage.
